extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary) and patent applicants/practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how to issue, withdraw, and process final rejections, reply periods, advisory actions, examiner's amendments, and transitional after-final submissions in patent prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection on first Office action (continuing/substitute applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of a new application may be finally rejected in the first Office action where (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims of the new application (1) are drawn to the same invention claimed in the earlier application, and (2) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraphs 7.41 or 7.41.03 as appropriate. A request for an interview prior to first action on a continuing or substitute application should ordinarily be granted. Do not use where amendments raised new issues/new matter or where statutory exceptions apply (see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection immediately following an RCE (37 CFR 1.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of an application for which a Request for Continued Examination (RCE) has been filed may be finally rejected in the action immediately subsequent to the filing of the RCE where all claims after entry of the 1.114 submission (A) are drawn to the same invention claimed in the application prior to the entry, and (B) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if entered prior to the filing of the RCE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply same principles as first-action final rejections (MPEP § 706.07(b)). Use appropriate form paragraph (e.g., 7.42.09). Note statutory and practice limitations (e.g., not made final if new ground necessitated by intervening law changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: When a first-action final rejection is improper
rubrics_metrics.description: A first Office action in a continuing/substitute application or an RCE may not be made final if it contains a new ground of rejection introduced by the examiner which was not necessitated by amendment to the claims nor based on information submitted in an IDS filed during the period set forth in 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(p). Also improper when a continuation-in-part contains claims with subject matter not present in the earlier application, or when material presented in the earlier application after final rejection was denied entry because new issues/new matter were raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: do not use the 'first action final' form paragraph if amendments were refused entry in the parent case on grounds of raising new issues/new matter. Be aware of reissue litigation and reexamination restrictions (SSP differences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for reply to a final rejection (shortened statutory period rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rejections setting a 3-month Shortened Statutory Period (SSP) should advise applicant that if a first reply is filed within 2 months of the final action, the shortened period will expire at 3 months from the final rejection or on the mailing date of the advisory action, whichever is later. In no event will the statutory period for reply expire later than six months from the mailing date of the final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraphs 7.39, 7.40, 7.41, etc., should be used to set the variable reply period. If the last day of the 2-month period falls on a weekend/holiday and applicant files on the next business day, it is deemed timely under 37 CFR 1.7(a). SSPs shorter than 3 months (e.g., reissue litigation, reexamination) are treated differently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory action handling and PTOL-303 usage
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply after final does not place the application in condition for allowance, the examiner should issue an Advisory Action (PTOL-303) indicating options for applicant to avoid abandonment (amendment placing application in condition for allowance; Notice of Appeal; or RCE), and specifying the applicable time period for reply (including whether the first reply was within two months).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check box 1.b) on PTOL-303 if applicant filed first reply within two months and the advisory action is used to set the 3-month SSP; otherwise check box 1.a). PTOL-303 must state that the statutory period for reply will not exceed six months from mailing date of final rejection. It also includes standardized sections for Notice of Appeal timing, reasons why proposed post-final amendments will not be entered, status of claims, IDS handling, and affidavit/evidence entry decisions (with citations to 37 CFR 1.116, 41.33, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation and consequences of extension fees (37 CFR 1.136(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Extension fees under 37 CFR 1.136(a) must be paid when applicant requires additional time beyond the SSP; the fee amount is calculated from either (1) the expiration date of the shortened statutory period originally set in the final Office action, or (2) as set in PTOL-303 when box 1.b) is checked (if applicable). The date on which the petition and appropriate extension fee are filed is the date for determining the period and amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension fees cannot be prorated for portions of a month. Any reply received by the Office later than three months after mailing of the final rejection, even if timely filed (with extension), may reduce any earned patent term adjustment (37 CFR 1.704(b)). If an advisory action is mailed after the 3-month period, the SSP may expire on the advisory action mailing date and fees are calculated from that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's amendments: timing, authorization, and fee rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a complete first reply is filed within 2 months of the final Office action, an examiner's amendment to place the application in condition for allowance may be made without payment of extension fees even if the amendment is made more than 3 months from the date of final action, provided the amendment is made within six months. If a complete first reply was not filed within 2 months, applicant's authorization to make such an amendment must be within the SSP or within an extended period obtained by petition and fee under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examiner's amendment cannot be made more than six months from the date of final action. Examiner's amendments limited to correcting formal matters first identified after a reply do not require extension fees. Telephone authorization to make a petition of record must be memorialized: record the person, date, deposit account number, length of extension, and fee amount using Form Paragraph 13.02.02. Office employees may not accept oral telephonic credit card instructions to charge patent process fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of finality when final rejection is premature
rubrics_metrics.description: If on reconsideration the primary examiner finds the final rejection to have been premature, the finality of the rejection should be withdrawn while the application is still pending; the examiner cannot withdraw final rejection once the application is abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form Paragraph 7.42 when withdrawing finality of the last Office action. After withdrawal, the next Office action may be made final if conditions of MPEP § 706.07(a) are met. Prematureness is a practice question and is reviewable only by petition under 37 CFR 1.181, not by appeal or Board complaint (see MPEP § 1002.02(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of final rejection generally (post-final amendments and new facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection that is not premature has been entered, it generally should not be withdrawn at applicant's request except on a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b). However, the examiner may withdraw a final rejection if new facts or reasons convince the examiner that previously rejected claims are allowable or patentable; the finality may also be withdrawn to apply a new ground of rejection in certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Withdrawal to enter a new ground of rejection should be limited to situations where a new reference either fully meets a claim or meets it except for differences shown to be completely obvious; do not withdraw merely to apply subsidiary, cumulative, or 'better' references. When finality is withdrawn, amendments filed after final rejection are ordinarily entered. New grounds of rejection made after filing an appeal brief require supervisory approval (MPEP § 1002.02(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing replies after final (consideration timing and requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replies after final should be processed and considered promptly. They should not be considered by the examiner unless filed within the SSP or accompanied by a petition for extension of time and the appropriate fee (37 CFR 1.17 and 1.136(a)). This requirement applies also to supplemental replies filed after the first reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution is reopened after a final Office action has been replied to, the finality of the previous Office action should be withdrawn to avoid abandonment and payment of extension fees. Formal matters first identified after a reply that require applicant action may be handled as Ex parte Quayle actions if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance, with no extension fees required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews and formal matters after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews may be conducted after expiration of the shortened statutory period for reply to a final Office action but within the six-month statutory period for reply without payment of an extension fee. Formal matters first identified after a reply may be required in an Ex parte Quayle action if the application is otherwise in condition for allowance; corrections of such formal matters do not require extension fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the distinction between substantive issues (which may require petition/fee or withdrawal of finality) and formal corrections (which can often be handled without fees).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional after-final practice (37 CFR 1.129(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants in applications (other than reissue or design) pending at least two years as of June 8, 1995 (effective filing date June 8, 1993 or earlier) are entitled to have a first submission entered and considered on the merits after final rejection if the first submission and the fee under 37 CFR 1.17(r) are filed prior to filing an appeal brief and prior to abandonment. The finality of the final rejection is automatically withdrawn upon timely filing and payment. A second submission and fee are similarly permitted once more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'submission' includes IDS, amendments to specification/claims/drawings, new substantive arguments, or new evidence but may not introduce new matter (35 U.S.C. 132). The transitional practice is only available to applications filed on or before June 8, 1995 and is not available for reissue/design applications or reexamination proceedings. Use Form Paragraph 7.41.01 to notify applicant. IDS previously refused because of 1.97(c)/(d) noncompliance may be treated as timely if compliant with 1.98 and fee rules (with special handling for submissions filed on/after 6/8/05 per 1.97(e)/1.17(p)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-final amendments and affidavits/evidence entry criteria (before/during appeal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed amendments filed after a final rejection but prior to filing a brief will not be entered if they: (a) raise new issues requiring further consideration/search, (b) raise the issue of new matter, (c) do not place application in better form for appeal by materially reducing/simplifying issues, or (d) present additional claims without canceling a corresponding number of finally rejected claims. Affidavits or other evidence filed after final must show 'good and sufficient reasons' why the evidence is necessary and was not earlier presented (37 CFR 1.116(e)), and may be refused entry under appeal rules (37 CFR 41.33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-303 sections list specific not-entered reasons and reference 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33(a)/(d)(1). If affidavit/evidence is entered, examiner must explain status of claims after entry. Amendments not in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121 should be handled with PTOL-324 Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment.
